case.diagnosis: Invasive papillary carcinoma of the breast
case.narrative: A breast papillary carcinoma subtype characterized by slow biological activity and gradual progression, typically luminal type, Nottingham grade 2, and low TNM stage. Compared with invasive ductal carcinoma, it shows more favorable pathology with lower tumor T stage, lower axillary lymph node metastasis rates (~11.6%–17.25% vs ~32.6%–50%), lower Ki-67, higher hormone receptor positivity, and lower HER2 amplification; larger tumor size and lymphovascular invasion are less prevalent. Reported case: 59-year-old with ~10-year natural history; large primary tumor (~10.4 × 7.2 × 3.5 cm) grew <2 cm over a decade without treatment, no distant metastases; IHC stable with ER/PR positive, HER2 (C-erbB2) negative. Genomic features in papillary carcinoma subtypes show similarities (loss of 16q; gain of 16p and 1q), fewer aberrations and minimal p53 expression; PIK3CA mutations in ~40% have been observed; transcriptomic differences relate to cell adhesion/migration genes. Organoid drug sensitivity testing in a papillary carcinoma case showed high efficacy of fulvestrant among tested endocrine therapies.
